summary.name: Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) guide
summary.one_liner: An Atlassian explainer on site reliability engineering, a discipline that applies software engineering to operations to keep systems reliable and scalable.
use_cases: Deciding whether an organization should adopt SRE
Defining reliability targets with SLIs, SLOs and error budgets
Comparing SRE, DevOps and traditional IT operations
Structuring an SRE team (embedded, centralized or hybrid)
Running blameless postmortems and incident response
Reducing repetitive operational toil through automation
summary.what_it_does: The page explains site reliability engineering as a discipline that applies software engineering to operations work to build and maintain reliable, scalable systems. It describes four pillars: measurement (SLIs, SLOs, SLAs and error budgets), response (incident management and sustainable on-call), learning (blameless postmortems), and improvement (toil reduction, automation and capacity planning). It compares SRE with traditional IT operations and DevOps in a table of focus, team structure, strengths and limitations. It also covers team structure options, leadership support, signs that an organization is ready to adopt SRE, and a phased implementation approach. Atlassian promotes its Jira Service Management product in several places.
notable: Describes the four SRE pillars: measurement, response, learning and improvement
Compares SRE, DevOps and traditional IT operations in a table
Covers embedded, centralized and hybrid SRE team structures
Includes Ben Treynor's definition of SRE from Google
caveats: Mostly a conceptual guide; it names Jira Service Management and Opsgenie as Atlassian products, with an Opsgenie migration notice before April 5th, 2027
Requires technical maturity, clear metrics and coding expertise, per the page
Implementation challenges include cultural resistance, hiring difficulty and managing toil
